dedupe_keys.name: hdm 4 highway development and management model for road maintenance and investment appraisal

description: HDM-4 (Highway Development and Management) is a software package for the analysis, planning, management and appraisal of road maintenance, improvements and investment decisions. The World Road Association (PIARC) holds its intellectual property, entrusted to it in 1998 by the stakeholders of the International Study of Highway Development and Management (ISOHDM); PIARC set up a service concession in 2004, awarded to HDMGlobal, a consortium centred on the University of Birmingham, and TRL Software now describes itself as the official distributor. TRL's page says HDM-4 supports operational management of highway networks, maintenance programming, funding estimates, budget allocation, whole-life network performance modelling, cost-benefit appraisal of new schemes, policy impact evaluation and economic impact analysis, and can be configured with data and calibration coefficients for a country or region. Coverage: road networks worldwide; TRL states users in over 90 countries, 70% of licences academic. Format and access: Windows desktop software, current version 2.12.02 (upgrade February 2024), with an HDM-Sentry module for data connectivity and exchange with pavement management systems such as TRL's iROADS; HDM-5 is being built. Cost: paid licences, quoted on request; prices were not read. Licence: proprietary. Caveats: the model relationships (pavement deterioration, road user costs) are described in documentation that was not read. Simulation uses: long-term road network condition and maintenance funding scenarios, including deterioration under changed climate or budgets. Related records: DG-QRAM (model-dg-qram-dangerous-goods-road-tunnel-risk), also a PIARC tool, assesses dangerous goods risk in road tunnels.
